login.subtitle: Keep images in your own GitHub repository or Cloudflare R2 bucket and share them with links.
login.step_repo: Create a public repository, for example {repo}:
login.step_repo_branch: Recommended: name its default branch gh-pages, so that PiCG and GitHub Pages use the same branch. For an existing repository, rename the branch on the repository's Branches page; PiCG follows the rename.
login.step_token: Create a fine-grained personal access token:
login.step_token_access: Repository access: Only select repositories, and select only the image repositories.
login.step_token_permission: Repository permissions: Contents, Read and write. Leave everything else at No access.
login.step_sign_in: Enter the token below and sign in.
login.from_legacy: The token and repositories saved by PicX or an earlier version of PiCG in this browser were found and filled in.
login.repos_hint: Names only, separated by commas or spaces; write name@branch to use a branch other than the default. Empty means {repo}.
login.repo_names_invalid: Enter repository names only, without the user name or a URL.
login.skip_message: The token is only kept obfuscated in the localStorage of your browser, so the everyday risk is low, but using a token with broad permissions for image hosting is a bad security habit: if it leaks, every repository it can reach is affected. This option exists because checking the permissions of each repository is slow when you have many of them. Do you understand the risk and want to continue?
login.storage_note: The token is kept in this browser in obfuscated form, which keeps it from being readable at a glance but is not encryption. GitHub does not show all permissions of a token, so the check cannot see extra permissions on the image repositories themselves; leave them at No access.

fail.invalid: This is not a valid fine-grained token (they start with github_pat_), or GitHub did not accept it.
fail.classic: This is a classic token, which can reach all your repositories. Create a fine-grained token instead.
fail.repo_missing: Repository {repo} was not found. Check the name, and that the token can access it.
fail.repo_blocked: GitHub has blocked {repo}, for example after a DMCA takedown, so it cannot hold images. Use another repository.
fail.no_write: The token cannot write to {repo}. Give it Contents: Read and write.
fail.other_write: The token can also write to {repo}. Limit its repository access to the image repositories.
fail.network: Could not reach GitHub. Check the connection and try again.
fail.rate_limit: GitHub's rate limit was reached. Wait a few minutes and try again.
fail.unexpected: GitHub answered the check with an unexpected error (HTTP {status}). Try again later.

login.create_branch_message: {repo} has no branch named {branch}. Create it from the default branch?
login.forget_message: {name} and its cached settings are removed from this device. The images stay where they are.

library.empty_hint: Drop, paste or pick images to upload them to this folder.
library.rename_hint: The image itself is not changed, only its name.
library.name_needs_extension: Keep an image extension such as .png or .webp.
library.name_taken: That name is already taken here.
library.delete_message: Links to deleted images stop working. The images stay in the repository's history.
library.path_invalid: There is no folder {name} here. Choose an existing folder, or create it with New folder.
library.truncated_r2: The bucket holds more than 100,000 files, so some are missing here.

import.title: Import from another repository
import.intro: Copies the images of another repository that are not here yet, keeping their paths. Up to 500 at a time.
import.not_found: That repository was not found, or the token cannot read it.
import.nothing: Nothing to import: every image is already here.

legacy.title: Settings from PicX or an earlier PiCG
legacy.found: Repository {repo} has settings saved by PicX or an earlier version of PiCG:
legacy.question: PiCG has translated them and is using them now. Save them in the new format and delete the old files?
legacy.decline_note: If not now, PiCG keeps working with these settings, but does not save settings to the repository until they are converted.

pages.off: GitHub Pages is off for this repository, so GitHub Pages links do not open. In the repository's Settings > Pages, choose Deploy from a branch, the {branch} branch and the / (root) folder, then Save.
pages.legacy: This repository still has a {legacy} branch, which earlier versions published to. PiCG no longer updates it, so if GitHub Pages publishes {legacy}, new images do not appear there. Recommended: delete {legacy}, then rename {branch} to {legacy} on the repository's Branches page; PiCG follows the rename. Otherwise, choose the {branch} branch and / (root) in Settings > Pages, then delete {legacy}. Either way this notice goes away.
pages.on: GitHub Pages is on and publishes at {url}. For new images to appear there, Pages must publish the {branch} branch; then they show up a few minutes after upload, with nothing to deploy.

settings.sign_in_first: Sign in to change upload, image and link settings.
settings.sync_blocked: This repository has settings saved by PicX or an earlier PiCG. Settings are not saved to the repository until they are converted.
settings.sync_error: Settings could not be saved to {repo}. They are kept on this device.
settings.replace_token_hint: The new token is checked like at sign-in.
settings.add_repo_hint: Write name@branch to use a branch other than the default. The token must include the repository in its access.
settings.repo_exists: That repository is already in the list.
settings.remove_repo_message: PiCG stops using {repo}. Nothing in the repository is deleted.
settings.repos_note: Each repository keeps its own settings in .picg/settings.toml.
settings.auto_upload_desc: Images are uploaded as soon as they are processed, without pressing Upload.
settings.subfolder_desc: Here uploads into the folder you are in. By date adds a folder named with the time format below. Named adds a folder you name.
settings.custom_hint: Uploads go to {path} below the current folder.
settings.time_format_desc: Uses date-fns tokens: yyyy year, MM month, dd day, HH hour. Slashes make nested folders.
settings.hash: Add a hash to file names
settings.hash_desc: A short fingerprint of the content, so names do not collide and the same image keeps the same name.
settings.prefix: Add a prefix to file names
settings.compress_desc: Re-encodes PNG, JPEG, WebP and AVIF images in the browser. If the result is larger than the original, the original is kept. GIF, SVG, ICO and BMP are uploaded as they are.
settings.watermark_desc: Drawn on PNG, JPEG, WebP and AVIF images. The size scales with the image width.
settings.domain_desc: Saving writes the CNAME file in the repository. Point the domain's DNS at GitHub Pages yourself.
settings.domain_invalid: Enter a domain such as img.example.com.
settings.template_https: The template must start with https://
settings.motion_reduced: Your system asks for reduced motion, so PiCG does not animate. Choose On to animate anyway.
settings.appearance_note: Theme, language and motion apply to this device only.
settings.branch_note: Images, settings and CNAME are read from and written to this branch. GitHub Pages publishes only one branch, so GitHub Pages links work only if Pages publishes this one. A branch named gh-pages is recommended.
settings.strip_metadata_desc: Removes EXIF and similar data, such as where and with which camera a photo was taken, from JPEG, PNG and WebP files uploaded without compression. Compressed and watermarked images never keep it. Orientation and colour profiles are kept.
settings.replace_keys_hint: The new keys are checked like at sign-in.
settings.buckets_note: Each bucket keeps its own settings in .picg/settings.toml.
settings.add_bucket_hint: A bucket of the same account that the token can read and write.
settings.bucket_invalid: Bucket names have 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
settings.bucket_exists: That bucket is already in the list.
settings.remove_bucket_message: PiCG stops using {bucket}. Nothing in the bucket is deleted.

tools.intro: These tools work in the browser and do not need a sign-in. Nothing is uploaded.

about.tagline: Image hosting on GitHub repositories, in the browser.
about.how_1: Images are stored in your own public GitHub repository, so you keep them and their history.
about.how_2: The library shows the repository's folders. Whatever you drop or paste goes into the folder you are in.
about.how_3: Images can be compressed and watermarked in the browser before upload.
about.how_4: After an upload, links are copied in the format you chose: plain, Markdown, HTML, BBCode or your own.
about.how_5: Links can point at GitHub, GitHub Pages (published from the same branch, nothing to deploy) or a CDN.
about.privacy: PiCG has no server. The app talks to GitHub directly from your browser, and the token never leaves it except to GitHub.
about.disclaimer: PiCG is provided "as is", without warranty of any kind. To the extent permitted by applicable law, the authors and contributors are not responsible for any data loss, token leak or other damage, and the code is not guaranteed to be 100% secure. Use it at your own risk.
about.content: Do not upload content that breaks the law or GitHub's terms. You are responsible for what you upload.
about.license: PiCG is open source under the Apache License 2.0.

login_r2.step_bucket: Create a bucket in Cloudflare R2:
login_r2.step_public: In the bucket's Settings, connect a custom domain, or turn on its public r2.dev address.
login_r2.step_public_dev: Cloudflare limits the r2.dev address and does not recommend it for production; a custom domain is better.
login_r2.step_cors: In the bucket's Settings, add this CORS policy, so that the browser lets PiCG talk to the bucket:
login_r2.step_token_permission: Permissions: Object Read & Write, applied to specific buckets only; select only the image bucket.
login_r2.step_token_keys: Copy its Access Key ID and Secret Access Key; Cloudflare shows the secret only once.
login_r2.s3_address_hint: As the bucket's Settings page shows it, ending with the bucket name.
login_r2.public_url_hint: The bucket's custom domain or r2.dev address. Links and thumbnails use it.
login_r2.keys_required: Enter the Access Key ID and the Secret Access Key.
login_r2.checking: Checking the keys with Cloudflare R2…
login_r2.storage_note: The keys are kept in this browser in obfuscated form, which keeps them from being readable at a glance but is not encryption. PiCG cannot see whether the token also reaches other buckets, so limit it to the image bucket.

fail.address: Enter the S3 API address of the bucket, such as https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/<BUCKET>.
fail.public_url: Enter the public address of the bucket, starting with https://.
fail.blocked: The browser blocked the request to bucket {bucket}. Most likely its CORS policy is missing or does not include this site: add the policy from step 3 and try again; it can take a minute to apply.
fail.network: Could not reach Cloudflare R2. Check the connection and try again.
fail.invalid: Cloudflare R2 did not accept the keys. Check the Access Key ID and the Secret Access Key.
fail.bucket_missing: Bucket {bucket} does not exist in this account.
fail.no_read: The keys cannot read bucket {bucket}. Give the token Object Read & Write on it.
fail.no_write: The keys cannot write to bucket {bucket}. Give the token Object Read & Write, not Read only.
fail.unexpected: Cloudflare R2 answered with an unexpected error (HTTP {status}).

r2_error.network: Could not reach Cloudflare R2. Check the connection and try again.
r2_error.rate_limit: Cloudflare R2 asked to slow down. Wait a moment and try again.
r2_error.unauthorized: Cloudflare R2 did not accept the keys. They may have been revoked; replace them in Settings.
r2_error.forbidden: The keys are not allowed to do this. Check the permissions of the token.
r2_error.not_found: Cloudflare R2 could not find it. It may have been moved or deleted.
r2_error.conflict: The file changed in the meantime, or the name is taken. Refresh and try again.
r2_error.too_large: The file is too large for Cloudflare R2.
r2_error.blocked: The browser blocked the request. The bucket's CORS policy probably does not include this site.
r2_error.server: Cloudflare R2 had a problem. Try again later.
r2_error.rename_incomplete: The image was copied to the new name, but the old one could not be deleted, so both are in the bucket.
r2_error.delete_incomplete: Some of the images could not be deleted. Refresh to see which are left.
